chunks.l2:
[tal-a03-v00] Then the supreme means of the great lord is praised, the supreme word indeed.

[tal-a03-v01] What was declared as mere light, the supreme Bhairava greatness, has only freedom distinguished there.

[tal-a03-v02] That light gives light-ness to all; nothing exists apart from it, and the universe appears as being.

[tal-a03-v03] Therefore that supreme lord, unbarred in his own self-space, reveals the spectacle of creation and destruction.

[tal-a03-v04] As earth, water, and so forth shine unmixed in a pure mirror, so world activities appear in one conscious lord.

[tal-a03-v05] Similar shining appears in eye, mirror, sky, and water; indeed, in pure form only form appears.

[tal-a03-v06] Though the hidden passionate woman touches with her breast-pots the mirror reflecting her beloved beautifully, she is not satisfied.

[tal-a03-v07] Indeed touch of it is not pure; form alone is so, because purity is extreme dense union of same kind.

[tal-a03-v08] Purity, as the guru taught, is the seeing capacity of the different arising from non-difference in self, for one who does not abandon self-light.

[tal-a03-v09] Purity is primary for the one consciousness-lord; elsewhere it is partial, by his will.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-:C3 śrītantrālokasya tṛtīyamāhnikam atha paraupayikaṃ praṇigadyate padamanuttarameva maheśituḥ prakāśamātraṃ yatproktaṃ bhairavīyaṃ paraṃ mahaḥ / tatra svatantratāmātramadhikaṃ pravivicyate yaḥ prakāśaḥ sa sarvasya prakāśatvaṃ prayacchati / na ca tadvyatirekyasti viśvaṃ sadvāvabhāsate ato@sau parameśānaḥ svātmavyomanyanargalaḥ / iyataḥ sṛṣṭisaṃhārāḍambarasya pradarśakaḥ nirmale makure yadvadbhānti bhūmijalādayaḥ / amiśrāstadvadekasmiṃścinnāthe viśvavṛttayaḥ sadṛśaṃ bhāti nayanadarpaṇāmbaravāriṣu / tathā hi nirmale rūpe rūpamevāvabhāsate pracchannarāgiṇī kāntapratibimbitasundaram / darpaṇaṃ kucakumbhābhyāṃ spṛśantyapi na tṛpyati na hi sparśo@sya vimalo rūpameva tathā yataḥ / nairmalyaṃ cātiniviḍasajātīyaikasaṃgatiḥ svasminnabhedādbhinnasya darśanakṣamataiva yā / atyaktasvaprakāśasya nairmalyaṃ tadgurūditam nairmalyaṃ mukhyamekasya saṃvinnāthasya sarvataḥ / aṃśāṃśikātaḥ kvāpyanyadvimalaṃ tattadicchayā

chunks.l2:
[tal-a03-v10] For beings, the obstructive body-maya nature belongs to them only; true-knowledge nature is non-obstructive.

[tal-a03-v11] Thus revealing an appearance of both forms, the boon-giver shines everywhere by image and reflection view.

[tal-a03-v12] Someone may argue that rays from the eyes strike a clear surface, bounce back, and thereby grasp one's own face; such a person is now questioned.

[tal-a03-v13] If the self, presiding over light outside the body, could know by that very light, then what need would there be for a mirror?

[tal-a03-v14] If the reversed rays became the graspers, the form would be seen on one's own face, not inside the mirror.

[tal-a03-v15] If it were really one's own face, that form would appear on one's own face, like touch, as 'mine'; but the mirror image is not tangible and has the nature of being only something seen.

[tal-a03-v16] The reflected image is only the shape of visible form; the real thing, joined with touch, smell, taste, and the rest, has those other qualities suppressed in the reflection.

[tal-a03-v17] Suppression is due to the absence of graspability, but that does not prove the thing is absent; and that non-graspability arises because there is no real contact with the object and because the image does not actually reside in the mirror.

[tal-a03-v18] For this reason, properties such as heaviness are not observed in the image; it is not actually situated in the mirror, which serves only as a means for seeing it.

[tal-a03-v19] Therefore, what appears does not exist there as something separate; the mirror is called its support only conventionally, while lamp, sight, and awareness are, in sequence, the real means of its appearance.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-bhāvānāṃ yatpratīghāti vapurmāyātmakaṃ hi tat / teṣāmevāsti sadvidyāmayaṃ tvapratighātakam tadevamubhayākāramavabhāsaṃ prakāśayan / vibhāti varado bimbapratibimbadṛśākhile yastvāha netratejāṃsi svacchātpratiphalantyalam / viparyasya svakaṃ vaktraṃ gṛhṇantīti sa pṛcchyate dehādanyatra yattejastadadhiṣṭhāturātmanaḥ / tenaiva tejasā jñatve ko@rthaḥ syāddarpaṇena tu viparyastaistu tejobhirgrāhakātmatvamāgataiḥ / rūpaṃ dṛśyeta vadane nije na makurāntare svamukhe sparśavaccaitadrūpaṃ bhāyānmametyalam / na tvasya spṛśyabhinnasya vedyaikāntasvarūpiṇaḥ rūpasaṃsthānamātraṃ tatsparśagandharasādibhiḥ / nyagbhūtaireva tadyuktaṃ vastu tatpratibimbitam nyagbhāvo grāhyatābhāvāttadabhāvo@pramāṇataḥ / sa cārthasaṃgamābhāvātso@pyādarśe@navasthiteḥ ata eva gurutvādirdharmo naitasya lakṣyate / nahyādarśe saṃsthito@sau taddṛṣṭau sa upāyakaḥ tasmāttu naiṣa bhedena yadbhāti tata ucyate / ādhārastatra tūpāyā dīpadṛksaṃvidaḥ kramāt

chunks.l2:
[tal-a03-v20] Lamp, eye, and cognition do not produce a separate mirror-like appearance, because they lack hardness and are supremely pure and clear on all sides.

[tal-a03-v21] The God of gods revealed this for the understanding of the deluded: a thing may appear even elsewhere than where it is, yet not fully or truly there.

[tal-a03-v22] The compassionate teacher explained that the image is not solid, not independent, and not simply stable or unstable; rather, it is the special power of some clear medium.

[tal-a03-v23] The teaching on the mirror declared that a reflection has no fixed place, no independent form, no time, no measure, no mutual contact, no removal, and no solidity; it is not simply unreal, nor does it have an essence of its own. By understanding this, delusion is dispelled.

[tal-a03-v24] In the account of reflection presented here, the reflection of sound is what is called an echo.

[tal-a03-v25] The echo is not produced by the original sound coming back, because although it is heard as if returning, the speaker does not hear it in that way and distant listeners may not hear the original sound at all.

[tal-a03-v26] Because an echo changes according to the hollows or openings it meets, the reflection of sound behaves like the reflection of a face or other visible form.

[tal-a03-v27] Just as a mirror shows the form of another object, an echo is heard as something spoken by another.

[tal-a03-v28] Because a reflection must face its original, the perceivers who stand between the source and the reflecting place are the ones who hear the echo.

[tal-a03-v29] A reflection can be perceived even without perceiving the original directly, just as one may see in a mirror the body of a beloved person standing behind oneself.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-dīpacakṣurvibodhānāṃ kāṭhinyābhāvataḥ param / sarvataścāpi nairmalyānna vibhādarśavatpṛthak etacca devadevena darśitaṃ bodhavṛddhaye / mūḍhānāṃ vastu bhavati tato@pyanyatra nāpyalam pratīghāti svatantraṃ no na sthāyyasthāyi cāpi na / svacchasyaivaiṣa kasyāpi mahimeti kṛpālunā na deśoṃ no rūpaṃ na ca samayayogo na parimā na cānyonyāsaṃgo na ca tadapahānirna ghanatā / na cāvastutvaṃ syānna ca kimapi sāraṃ nijamiti dhruvaṃ mohaḥ śāmyediti niradiśaddarpaṇavidhiḥ itthaṃ pradarśite@mutra pratibimbanavartmani / śabdasya pratibimbaṃ yat pratiśrutketi bhaṇyate na cāsau śabdajaḥ śabda āgacchattvena saṃśravāt / tenaiva vaktrā dūrasthaiḥ śabdasyāśravaṇādapi piṭhirādipidhānāṃśaviśiṣṭachidrasaṃgatau / citratvāccāsya śabdasya pratibimbaṃ mukhādivat idamanyasya vedyasya rūpamityavabhāsate / yathādarśe tathā kenāpyuktamākarṇaye tviti niyamādbimbasāṃmukhyaṃ pratibimbasya yattataḥ / tanmadhyagāḥ pramātāraḥ śṛṇvanti pratiśabdakam mukhyagrahaṃ tvapi vinā pratibimbagraho bhavet / svapaścātsthaṃ priyaṃ paśyeṭṭaṅkitaṃ mukure vapuḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a03-v30] Facingness is explained as the reflection's being situated in non-difference from the mirror-like condition in which it appears.

[tal-a03-v31] Therefore, in the hollow space of a well or jar, the speaker's space is reflected together with sound and appears as if another speaker were there.

[tal-a03-v32] Just as someone standing behind a mirror does not directly know the face, someone standing behind such a reflecting space does not directly know the original sound.

[tal-a03-v33] An unmanifest sound is not reflected; its manifestation and hearing occur at the same time, in the second moment.

[tal-a03-v34] In that moment, the sound's being reflected and its being heard occur at the same time, just as one does not ascertain a hand and its shadow at different times.

[tal-a03-v35] Now that the true nature of reflection has been shown here, we return to the main topic, for reflection properly applies there.

[tal-a03-v36] Sound is reflected beautifully in space, and touch too can appear as something external, like a blow, pain, or cold, yet it agitates one's own body because it is a reflection.

[tal-a03-v37] This reflected touch is not the primary one, because it does not reveal an independent chain of effects of its own.

[tal-a03-v38] In the same way, smell appears within the organ of smell, and taste appears clearly in the moisture of the mouth.

[tal-a03-v39] Just as a reflected form is not seen without the eyes, taste, touch, fragrance, and the rest are not perceived without their proper sense organs, even if they are present.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-sāṃmukhyaṃ cocyate tādṛgdarpaṇābhedasaṃsthiteḥ ataḥ kūpādipiṭhirākāśe tatpratibimbitam / vaktrākāśaṃ saśabdaṃ sadbhāti tatparavaktavat yathā cādarśapāścātyabhāgastho vetti no mukham / tathā tathāvidhākāśapaścātstho vetti na dhvanim śabdo na cānabhivyaktaḥ pratibimbati taddhruvam / abhivyaktiśrutī tasya samakālaṃ dvitīyake kṣaṇe tu pratibimbatvaṃ śrutiśca samakālikā / tulyakālaṃ hi no hastatacchāyārūpaniścayaḥ itthaṃ pradarśite@mutra pratibimbasatattvake / prakṛtaṃ brūmahe tatra pratibimbanamarhati śabdo nabhasi sānande sparśadhāmani sundaraḥ / sparśo@nyo@pi dṛḍhāghātaśūlaśītādikodbhavaḥ / parasthaḥ pratibimbatvātsvadehoddhūlanākaraḥ na caiṣa mukhyastatkāryapāramparyāprakāśanāt evaṃ ghrāṇāntare gandho raso dantodake sphuṭaḥ yathā ca rūpaṃ pratibimbitaṃ dṛśorna cakṣuṣānyena vinā hi lakṣyate / tathā rasasparśanasaurabhādikaṃ na lakṣyate@kṣeṇa vinā sthitaṃ tvapi

chunks.l2:
[tal-a03-v40] The object of the cognition of an external touch is not located inside the inner field of touch.

[tal-a03-v41] When one's nearby sense organs and inner instruments are properly engaged, the reflection received in the sense organ produces a corresponding activity.

[tal-a03-v42] An action does not arise from a remembered mental object, because such action truly belongs to the present. Therefore, the excellent touch is situated in that sense organ, having arrived there and being known, and it acts accordingly in the present.

[tal-a03-v43] When an external object is impossible, that same excellent touch, reflected within one's own self, produces that pleasurable sensation. It does so within some continuum of subtle channels.

[tal-a03-v44] Therefore, by offering the universe as his own self in the mirror of consciousness, this declares the pure universal nature of the Lord.

[tal-a03-v45] Just as smell, form, touch, taste, and other qualities, when reflected, shine in a sword by taking on the coloring of that support, like a face and other images reflected there.

[tal-a03-v46] Likewise, this universe, reflected in consciousness, should be understood to rest upon its expansive qualities, such as luminosity and freedom.

[tal-a03-v47] Just as a reflection from all sides may appear in a crystal that is clear on all sides, so too reflections appear in consciousness, which possesses complete clarity.

[tal-a03-v48] Absolute transparency is the non-manifestation of one's own form. Therefore consciousness is the most transparent, unlike a jewel, which grasps and displays its own form.

[tal-a03-v49] A reflection is projected by an external original image, but if everything is a reflection of consciousness itself, what external original image could possibly remain?
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-na cāntare sparśanadhāmani sthitaṃ bahiḥspṛśonyākṣadhiyaḥ sa gocaraḥ ato@ntikasthasvakatādṛgindriyaprayojanāntaḥkaraṇairyadā kṛtā / tadā tadāttaṃ pratibimbamindriye svakāṃ kriyāṃ sūyata eva tādṛśīm na tu smṛtānmānasagocarādṛtā bhavetkriyā sā kila vartamānataḥ / ataḥ sthitaḥ sparśavarastadindriye samāgataḥ sanviditastathākriyaḥ asaṃbhave bāhyagatasya tādṛśaḥ sva eva tasminpratibimbitastathā / karoti tāṃ sparśavaraḥ sukhātmikāṃ sa cāpi kasyāmapi nāḍisaṃtatau tena saṃvittimakure viśvamātmānamarpayat / nāthasya vadate@muṣya vimalāṃ viśvarūpatām yathā ca gandharūpaspṛgrasādyāḥ pratibimbitāḥ / tadādhāroparāgeṇa bhānti khaṅge mukhādivat tathā viśvamidaṃ bodhe pratibimbitamāśrayet / prakāśatvasvatantratvaprabhṛtiṃ dharmavistaram yathā ca sarvataḥ svacche sphaṭike sarvato bhavet / pratibimbaṃ tathā bodhe sarvataḥ svacchatājuṣi atyantasvacchatā sā yatsvākṛtyanavabhāsanam / ataḥ svacchatamo bodho na ratnaṃ tvākṛtigrahāt pratibimbaṃ ca bimbena bāhyasthena samarpyate / tasyaiva pratibimbatve kiṃ bimbamavaśiṣyatām

chunks.l2:
[tal-a03-v50] Even if some cause is designated as an external original image, it too becomes a reflection in consciousness; otherwise, outside of consciousness, it would be unreal.

[tal-a03-v51] Thus, protected by the firm weapon of the logic of one's own awareness, the sovereignty of reflection alone expands everywhere.

[tal-a03-v52] An objector asks how a reflection can exist without an original image. The reply is: what can we do, for it is seen? The objector is then challenged to identify that supposed original image.

[tal-a03-v53] It is not so, because the supposed original lacks the required definition. What is truly called an original image is something unmixed with others, independent, and truly appearing, just like a face.

[tal-a03-v54] They define the nature of a reflection as resembling another form without abandoning its own nature, like reflections seen on a sword, a mirror, or a flat surface.

[tal-a03-v55] And it is said by the Buddhists that even if external objects exist, cognition is one because it perceives many; it takes on forms resembling many, but it does not itself become many.

[tal-a03-v56] But what, then, is the definition of a reflection? It is stated as the impossible manifestation of difference from its substrate due to the unfitness for mixing with another, just as a face appears in a mirror.

[tal-a03-v57] This universe, beginning with the supreme reality, is mixed with consciousness and cannot be manifested as different from consciousness; why, then, should it not be called a reflection in consciousness?

[tal-a03-v58] If this arrangement of the definition is arbitrary, then let the universe be called the original image. Wise people are concerned with reality itself, not with conventional terminology.

[tal-a03-v59] But surely a reflection cannot exist without an original image? What of that? In a reflection, the original image does not exist as a separate entity, for it exists only in identity with it.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-yadvāpi kāraṇaṃ kiṃcidbimbatvenābhiṣicyate / tadapi pratibimbatvameti bodhe@nyathā tvasat itthametatsvasaṃvittidṛḍhanyāyāstrarakṣitam / sāmrājyameva viśvatra pratibimbasya jṛmbhate nanu bimbasya virahe pratibimbaṃ kathaṃ bhavet / kiṃ kurmo dṛśyate taddhi nanu tadbimbamucyatām naivaṃ tallakṣaṇābhāvādbimbaṃ kila kimucyate / anyāmiśraṃ svatantraṃ sadbhāsamānaṃ mukhaṃ yathā svarūpānapahānena pararūpasadṛkṣatām / pratibimbātmatāmāhuḥ khaḍgādarśatalādivat uktaṃ ca sati bāhye@pi dhīrekānekavedanāt / anekasadṛśākārā na tvaneketi saugataiḥ nanvitthaṃ pratibimbasya lakṣaṇaṃ kiṃ taducyate / anyavyāmiśraṇāyogāttadbhedāśakyabhāsanam / pratibimbamiti prāhurdarpaṇe vadanaṃ yathā bodhamiśramidaṃ bodhādbhedenāśakyabhāsanam / paratattvādi bodhe kiṃ pratibimbaṃ na bhaṇyate lakṣaṇasya vyavasthaiṣākasmāccedbimbamucyatām / prājñā vastuni yujyante na tu sāmayike dhvanau nanu na pratibimbasya vinā bimbaṃ bhavetsthitiḥ / kiṃ tataḥ pratibimbe hi bimbaṃ tādātmyavṛtti na

chunks.l2:
[tal-a03-v60] So, even if this stated definition is impossible, there is no loss in taking it as a mere cause; rather, the question comes to rest there.

[tal-a03-v61] Even in the case of what is called an instrumental cause, and not a material one, instrumental causes cannot in any way be possible at any time or place.

[tal-a03-v62] For this very reason, when light is present before one, the form of the beloved may appear vividly transferred there through memory and similar instrumental triggers.

[tal-a03-v63] Otherwise, why would the beloved, who is actually separated, appear as present in consciousness? Consciousness does not go out in front to reach that separation.

[tal-a03-v64] Therefore, let there be some inner factor called intellect, in which appearances arise clearly by division, as in imagination and in the seeing of dreams.

[tal-a03-v65] Therefore, let the Lord's powers be the instrumental cause in such cases. Thus this whole universe is a pure reflection in the clear sky of Bhairava-consciousness, not by the grace of anything else.

[tal-a03-v66] That power of the Lord, independent of anything else, by which he is the self of the universe, is declared to be the supreme, unsurpassed goddess Pratibhā.

[tal-a03-v67] Of this Lord Akula, the supreme power is Kaulikī, who shines in the spreading forth of Kula; the Lord is never separated from her.

[tal-a03-v68] The pure united form of those two is remembered as saṃghaṭṭa. That same union is called the power of bliss, because from it the universe is emitted.

[tal-a03-v69] This goddess is declared to be the principle beyond the supreme and the non-supreme. She is its essence and its heart; that supreme emission is the Lord.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-ataśca lakṣaṇasyāsya proktasya tadasaṃbhave / na hānirhetumātre tu praśno@yaṃ paryavasyati tatrāpi ca nimittākhye nopādāne kathaṃcana / nimittakāraṇānāṃ ca kadācitkvāpi saṃbhavaḥ ata eva purovartinyāloke smaraṇādinā / nimittena ghanenāstu saṃkrāntadayitākṛtiḥ anyathā saṃvidārūḍhā kāntā vicchedayoginī / kasmādbhāti na vai saṃvid vicchedaṃ purato gatā ata evāntaraṃ kiṃciddhīsaṃjñaṃ bhavatu sphuṭam / yatrāsya vicchidā bhānaṃ saṃkalpasvapnadarśane ato nimittaṃ devasya śaktayaḥ santu tādṛśe / itthaṃ viśvamidaṃ nāthe bhairavīyacidambare / pratibimbamalaṃ svacche na khalvanyaprasādataḥ ananyāpekṣitā yāsya viśvātmatvaṃ prati prabhoḥ / tāṃ parāṃ pratibhāṃ devīṃ saṃgirante hyanuttarām akulasyāsya devasya kulaprathanaśālinī / kaulikī sā parā śaktiraviyukto yayā prabhuḥ tayoryadyāmalaṃ rūpaṃ sa saṃghaṭṭa iti smṛtaḥ / ānandaśaktiḥ saivoktā yato viśvaṃ visṛjyate parāparātparaṃ tattvaṃ saiṣā devī nigadyate / tatsāraṃ tacca hṛdayaṃ sa visargaḥ paraḥ prabhuḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a03-v70] In the Devīyāmala scripture she is described as Kālakarṣiṇī, and likewise in the Mahāḍāmaraka rite the glorious supreme goddess is placed at the head.

[tal-a03-v71] In the Śrīpūrva scripture she is described as the true nature of the mothers, as that reflective awareness of being consciousness within this union.

[tal-a03-v72] The supreme will-power of the fierce powers is the lord; that same power, when agitated in form, becomes the ruler.

[tal-a03-v73] Then fierce supreme goddesses are born as guides of the shaiva path; self-reflection, formerly the single hero, arises.

[tal-a03-v74] Established by knowledge-power, this supreme-lower goddess, whose self unfolds the knowable universe, creates the fierce circle of mothers.

[tal-a03-v75] It continuously creates the lamp of pure and impure paths; when the knowable portion comes with rising agitation from strength.

[tal-a03-v76] Deficiency-appearance arises in pure consciousness; then the established knowable class is called the beginning of stability.

[tal-a03-v77] This establishment is the grasp of varied forms in the ocean of awareness; yogis collect this seed of seed-arrangement.

[tal-a03-v78] Will-power, said to be two-formed and agitated or unagitated, indeed rests in the self through the duality of objects.

[tal-a03-v79] By the quickly shining power of fire-form, desired attainment occurs through stability in the earth-self.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-devīyāmalaśāstre sā kathitā kālakarṣiṇī / mahāḍāmarake yāge śrīparā mastake tathā śrīpūrvaśāstre sā mātṛsadbhāvatvena varṇitā / saṃghaṭṭe@smiṃścidātmatvādyattatpratyavamarśanam icchāśaktiraghorāṇāṃ śaktīnāṃ sā parā prabhuḥ / saiva prakṣubdharūpā cedīśitrī saṃprajāyate tadā ghorāḥ parā devyo jātāḥ śaivādhvadaiśikāḥ / svātmapratyavamarśo yaḥ prāgabhūdekavīrakaḥ jñātavyaviśvonmeṣātmā jñānaśaktitayā sthitaḥ / iyaṃ parāparā devī ghorāṃ yā mātṛmaṇḍalīm sṛjatyavirataṃ śuddhāśuddhamārgaikadīpikām / jñeyāṃśaḥ pronmiṣankṣobhaṃ yadaiti balavattvataḥ ūnatābhāsanaṃ saṃvinmātratve jāyate tadā / rūḍhaṃ tajjñeyavargasya sthitiprārambha ucyate rūḍhireṣā vibodhābdheścitrākāraparigrahaḥ / idaṃ tadbījasaṃdarbhabījaṃ cinvanti yoginaḥ icchāśaktirdvirūpoktā kṣubhitākṣubhitā ca yā / iṣyamāṇaṃ hi sā vastudvairūpyeṇātmani śrayet aciradyutibhāsinyā śaktyā jvalanarūpayā / iṣyamāṇasamāpattiḥ sthairyeṇātha dharātmanā

chunks.l2:
[tal-a03-v80] Although this is knowable in the unfolding power abundantly, nevertheless that is the place of glory, not the eastern birth-place.

[tal-a03-v81] Thus from will-power they say four-formed supreme nectar; because there is no inner agitation, this is not the seed of anyone.

[tal-a03-v82] Agitating-nature, seed-nature, support of agitation, and womb-nature are named; the form of consciousness is agitated and also agitates.

[tal-a03-v83] Agitation would be the knowable quality; agitating is its exclusion, while the inner undivided one-seed desire to emit remains.

[tal-a03-v84] Agitation in that will is the appearance of truth-will; they know agitating, and having attained unity, that will becomes effective.

[tal-a03-v85] The sons of Shri Somananda call this support of agitation the undifferentiated distinctness of the beginnings of consciousness.

[tal-a03-v86] Whatever is only knowable is that seed; by union, seedness is in sound; that same seed's desire to emit is the origin from which this grasped shining different form of consciousness-self arises.

[tal-a03-v87] This is agitation; agitating, however, expels the silent other-mother-going and the sudden indifference-part from consciousness by force.

[tal-a03-v88] Although born, that desire to emit becomes accomplished from the unity of other reflection; thus the support of agitation is proclaimed.

[tal-a03-v89] Then that knowable interval desires a different form from the universe-seed; all external reflection will manifest.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-unmeṣaśaktāvastyetajjñeyaṃ yadyapi bhūyasā / tathāpi vibhavasthānaṃ sā na tu prācyajanmabhūḥ icchāśakterataḥ prāhuścātūrūpyaṃ parāmṛtam / kṣobhāntarasyāsadbhāvānnedaṃ bījaṃ ca kasyacit prakṣobhakatvaṃ bījatvaṃ kṣobhādhāraśca yonitā / kṣobhakaṃ saṃvido rūpaṃ kṣubhyati kṣobhayatyapi kṣobhaḥ syājjñeyadharmatvaṃ kṣobhaṇā tadbahiṣkṛtiḥ / antaḥsthaviśvābhinnaikabījāṃśavisisṛkṣutā kṣobho@tadicche tattvecchābhāsanaṃ kṣobhaṇāṃ viduḥ / yadaikyāpattimāsādya tadicchā kṛtinī bhavet kṣobhādhāramimaṃ prāhuḥ śrīsomānandaputrakāḥ / saṃvidāmīṣaṇādīnāmanudbhinnaviśeṣakam yajjñeyamātraṃ tadbījaṃ yadyogādbījatā svare / tasya bījasya saivoktā visisṛkṣā ya udbhavaḥ / yato grāhyamidaṃ bhāsyadbhinnakalpaṃ cidātmanaḥ eṣa kṣobhaḥ kṣobhaṇā tu tūṣṇīṃbhūtānyamātṛgam / haṭhādyadaudāsīnyāṃśacyāvanaṃ saṃvido balāt jātāpi visisṛkṣāsau yadvimarśāntaraikyataḥ / kṛtārthā jāyate kṣobhādhāro@traitatprakīrtitam tatastadāntaraṃ jñeyaṃ bhinnakalpatvamicchati / viśvabījādataḥ sarva bāhyaṃ bimbaṃ vivartsyati

chunks.l2:
[tal-a03-v90] The true nature of the agitated-agitating state has been shown by me, as spoken by Shri Maheshvara, by the grace of the guru.

[tal-a03-v91] We speak of the subject; this is not seed, the four letters, nor does it attain the status of support of agitation.

[tal-a03-v92] In the self only, by rest, that spoken immortal nature; thus the previously spoken fivefold is mutual.

[tal-a03-v93] From the mutual mixing of rising varied forms, the supreme higher vibration and bliss rise together.

[tal-a03-v94] From that collision of will-unfolding going to great variety, supreme bliss-consciousness is in will-power when employed.

[tal-a03-v95] Thus the triangle is called beautiful emission-bliss; supreme bliss-powers attain establishment there.

[tal-a03-v96] When two triangles join, the configuration moves into a six-spoked state; yet even in that unfolding, it goes again into absorption in that same reality.

[tal-a03-v97] The stirring that arises in the unfolding of will, mutually interacting, clearly manifests the form of the power of action; this is also said of that movement.

[tal-a03-v98] Those two powers indeed share that same form and do not stand otherwise. But how can unsurpassedness and bliss, which by their own nature are free from division, appear in this way?

[tal-a03-v99] How can those two, free from division, take on such variegation within their own self? Listen: this Lord of consciousness is by nature unlimited.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-kṣobhyakṣobhakabhāvasya satattvaṃ darśitaṃ mayā / śrīmanmaheśvareṇoktaṃ guruṇā yatprasādataḥ prakṛtaṃ brūmahe nedaṃ bījaṃ varṇacatuṣṭayam / nāpi yoniryato naitatkṣobhādhāratvamṛcchati ātmanyeva ca viśrāntyā tatproktamamṛtātmakam / itthaṃ prāguditaṃ yattatpañcakaṃ tatparasparam ucchaladvividhākāramanyonyavyatimiśraṇāt / yo@nuttaraḥ paraḥ spando yaścānandaḥ samucchalan tāvicchonmeṣasaṃghaṭṭādgacchato@tivicitratām / anuttarānandacitī icchāśaktau niyojite trikoṇamiti tatprāhurvisargāmodasundaram / anuttarānandaśaktī tatra rūḍhimupāgate trikoṇadvitvayogena vrajataḥ ṣaḍarasthitim / ta evonmeṣayoge@pi punastanmayatāṃ gate kriyāśakteḥ sphuṭaṃ rūpamabhivyaṅktaḥ parasparam / icchonmeṣagataḥ kṣobho yaḥ proktastadgaterapi te eva śaktī tādrūpyabhāginyau nānyathāsthite / nanvanuttaratānandau svātmanā bhedavarjitau kathametāvatīmenāṃ vaicitrīṃ svātmani śritau / śṛṇu tāvadayaṃ saṃvinnātho@parimitātmakaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a03-v100] If the great Lord, master of the dissolution and arising of endless varieties of power, were to remain in only one form, then what would follow?

[tal-a03-v101] He would abandon his great-lordship and his nature as consciousness, like a pot or any other finite thing. For limited luminosity is indeed the defining mark of the inert.

[tal-a03-v102] Awareness is distinct from the inert because it cannot be measured. Therefore, his own powers surge up like waves in the great ocean of awareness.

[tal-a03-v103] Like waves, they take on the variegation of their own self-union. That mutual diversity of the powers is the diversity of their own inner union.

[tal-a03-v104] They declare this very diversity to be the supreme, clear body of the power of action, in that fourteenth abode where the three powers have become manifest.

[tal-a03-v105] Therefore the Teacher declared this to be the trident in the Śrīpūrva teaching, and teachers who see reality have also called it stainless.

[tal-a03-v106] The power-holder seems affected because will, knowledge, and action appear separately; yet power itself is never affected by anything.

[tal-a03-v107] That same triad, through the power-holder's own modes such as willing and the rest, appears clearly; but when it shines forth in unity, then it does so as one.

[tal-a03-v108] Because the three powers cannot be grasped by any one-sided condition and mutually resist such limitation, they become a single vibrant trident. The yogi who quickly becomes absorbed in that trident becomes stainless.

[tal-a03-v109] In this way, the octad that begins from the supreme nectar state, when divided through Brahmi and the other forms, clearly expands into eight octads.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-anantaśaktivaicitryalayodayakaleśvaraḥ / asthāsyadekarūpeṇa vapuṣā cenmaheśvaraḥ maheśvaratvaṃ saṃvittvaṃ tadatyakṣyaddhaṭādivat / paricchinnaprakāśatvaṃ jaḍasya kila lakṣaṇam jaḍādvilakṣaṇo bodho yato na parimīyate / tena bodhamahasindhorullāsinyaḥ svaśaktayaḥ āśrayantyūrmaya iva svātmasaṃghaṭṭacitratām / svātmasaṃghaṭṭavaicitryaṃ śaktīnāṃ yatparasparam etadeva paraṃ prāhuḥ kriyāśakteḥ sphuṭaṃ vapuḥ / asmiṃścaturdaśe dhāmni sphuṭībhūtatriśaktike triśūlatvamataḥ prāha śāstā śrīpūrvaśāsane / nirañjanamidaṃ coktaṃ gurubhistattvadarśibhiḥ śaktimānañjyate yasmānna śaktirjātu kenacit / icchā jñānaṃ kriyā ceti yatpṛthakpṛthagañjyate tadeva śaktimatsvaiḥ svairiṣyamāṇādikaiḥ sphuṭam / etattritayamaikyena yadā tu prasphurettadā na kenacidupādheyaṃ svasvavipratiṣedhataḥ / lolībhūtamataḥ śaktitritayaṃ tattriśūlakam / yasminnāśu samāveśādbhavedyogī nirañjanaḥ itthaṃ parāmṛtapadādārabhyāṣṭakamīdṛśam / brāhmyādirūpasaṃbhedādyātyaṣṭāṣṭakatāṃ sphuṭam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a03-v110] Here the supreme power, even while making her own body manifest, takes the form of bindu because of the stain associated with the knowable aspect.

[tal-a03-v111] When the power of action has arisen in the abode of moon, sun, and fire, the undivided light that is present there is, for us, the supreme bindu.

[tal-a03-v112] And in the teaching on the protection of the principles, the supreme Lord said that the bindu stands within the circle of the heart-lotus and has a nature consisting of the human, power, and Shiva.

[tal-a03-v113] The bindu should be understood, through the distinction of dissolution, as pure and delivering. It is that sound whose nature is nada and which is present in all beings.

[tal-a03-v114] Though described by divisions of below and above, it remains without activity. Whatever variety appears, such as soothing or sharp qualities and white or red colors, belongs to that apparent diversity.

[tal-a03-v115] That light is in itself independent of those variations, as the teacher said. Neither the sun, nor the moon, nor even fire illuminates it.

[tal-a03-v116] Sun, moon, and fire have no splendor of their own apart from that light. Rather, it is consciousness that shines in this way.

[tal-a03-v117] Joined with varied conditions that arise from its own freedom, the one light takes on an inner variety, such as sharpness and other qualities.

[tal-a03-v118] Even the sun, which is hard to look at, becomes delightful to the eyes when its light falls on water. See how powerful a conditioning medium can be.

[tal-a03-v119] The light seen in the sun and other things is stained by limiting conditions, and therefore it depends on the Maheshvara light, the light of consciousness itself.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-atrānuttaraśaktiḥ sā svaṃ vapuḥ prakaṭasthitam / kurvantyapi jñeyakalākāluṣyādvindurūpiṇī uditāyāṃ kriyāśaktau somasūryāgnidhāmani / avibhāgaḥ prakāśo yaḥ sa binduḥ paramo hi naḥ tattvarakṣāvidhāne ca taduktaṃ parameśinā / hṛtpadmamaṇḍalāntaḥstho naraśaktiśivātmakaḥ boddhavyo layabhedena vindurvimalatārakaḥ / yo@sau nādātmakaḥ śabdaḥ sarvaprāṇiṣvavasthitaḥ adha+ūrdhvavibhāgena niṣkriyeṇāvatiṣṭhate / hlādataikṣṇyādi vaicitryaṃ sitaraktādikaṃ ca yat svayaṃ tannirapekṣo@sau prakāśo gururāha ca / yanna sūryo na vā somo nāgnirbhāsayate@pi ca na cārkasomavahnīnāṃ tatprakāśādvinā mahaḥ / kimapyasti nijaṃ kiṃ tu saṃviditthaṃ prakāśate svasvātantryaprabhāvodyadvicitropādhisaṃgataḥ / prakāśo yāti taikṣṇyādimavāntaravicitratām durdarśano@pi gharmāṃśuḥ patitaḥ pāthasāṃ pathi / netrānandatvamabhyeti paśyopādheḥ prabhāvitām sūryādiṣu prakāśo@sāvupādhikaluṣīkṛtaḥ / saṃvitprakāśaṃ māheśamata eva hyapekṣate

chunks.l2:
[tal-a03-v120] Clearly manifest mere light is called the sun. That aspect which pours forth the essential content of what is to be illuminated is called the moon.

[tal-a03-v121] They call the sun the means of knowing and the moon the object to be known. Though never separated from each other, the two also stand as independent.

[tal-a03-v122] When this pair, as enjoyer and enjoyed, turns toward each other, there arises a blazing form of consciousness that is proclaimed as fire.

[tal-a03-v123] The supreme principle of fire is nothing other than the knower's own reality. It is consciousness itself, not dependent on anything else because it is identical with what is to be known.

[tal-a03-v124] Because of its freedom, consciousness is called the knower. It appears varied through differences among knowables, expanded by the diverse appearances of objects that arise on the moon side and are taken up by the fire aspect.

[tal-a03-v125] For this reason the great Lord called this fire Citrabhanu. The status of consciousness is entirely independent of the whole set of means that begin with the knowable.

[tal-a03-v126] Consciousness stands as the immediate sense, 'I am the knower.' But one who knows like a person who merely knows scripture is not truly knowing in essence, because that knowledge depends on experienced objects rather than on its own self-form.

[tal-a03-v127] That is not true knowership which depends on a pure knowable or anything similar. In such a state, the term knowership is used only in a secondary sense, because of a certain fitness.

[tal-a03-v128] That dependent knowing is only a kind of measuring, constructed by the limited knower. Consciousness, even when it surges forth, is not divided by temporal sequence.

[tal-a03-v129] As soon as consciousness arises, it is already full and contains within itself the knower, the known, and the rest. Ordinary actions like cooking, by contrast, unfold in sequence because they are limited by time.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-prakāśamātraṃ suvyaktaṃ sūrya ityucyate sphuṭam / prakāśyavastusārāṃśavarṣi tatsoma ucyate sūrya pramāṇamityāhuḥ somaṃ meyaṃ pracakṣate / anyonyamaviyuktau tau svatantrāvapyubhau sthitau bhoktṛbhogyobhayātmaitadanyonyonmukhatāṃ gatam / tato jvalanacidrūpaṃ citrabhānuḥ prakīrtitaḥ yo@yaṃ vahneḥ paraṃ tattvaṃ pramāturidameva tat / saṃvideva tu vijñeyatādātmyādanapekṣiṇī svatantratvātpramātoktā vicitro jñeyabhedataḥ / somāṃśadāhyavastūtthavaicitryābhāsabṛṃhitaḥ tata evāgniruditaścitrabhānurmaheśinā / jñeyādyupāyasaṃghātanirapekṣaiva saṃvidaḥ sthitirmātāhamasmīti jñātā śāstrajñavadyataḥ / ajña eva yato jñātānubhavātmā na rūpataḥ na tu sā jñātṛtā yasyāṃ śuddhajñeyādyapekṣate / tasyāṃ daśāyāṃ jñātṛtvamucyate yogyatāvaśāt mānataiva tu sā prācyapramātṛparikalpitā / ucchalantyapi saṃvittiḥ kālakramavivarjanāt uditaiva satī pūrṇā mātṛmeyādirūpiṇī / pākādistu kriyā kālaparicchedātkramocitā

chunks.l2:
[tal-a03-v130] Even if one thinks of an action as ending in a final moment, that alone does not make it the completed act of cooking. In this way, the principle of light is established as having the nature of moon, sun, and fire.

[tal-a03-v131] Even so, the primary nature of these three is not removed: they remain mere light. Of these, the first, short form is called the sun.

[tal-a03-v132] Because of long rest arising from stirring and bliss, it is called Soma. That supreme state, named Pluta, is established beyond the bliss of Soma.

[tal-a03-v133] Those skilled in scripture call that light-natured state fiery. Here, when the three abodes are established, what remains is mere light.

[tal-a03-v134] In scripture this is spoken of as the bindu and is regarded as the Shiva-bindu. It is indeed other than the letter ma, bearing only its shadow.

[tal-a03-v135] Ra, la, and ha become established in the forms of ṣa, ṇ, ṭha, and visarga, just as the vowel i becomes another vowel through the shadow of a part of ra.

[tal-a03-v136] In the same way, from the great Lord arises another principle. Even while appearing as a vowel in two ways, that inner desire to emit within him is declared to be the supreme Kauliki power.

[tal-a03-v137] That very same power, through the force of stirring, certainly becomes visarga. This is said in the Trishiras scripture in the discussion that concludes with the pervasion of kala.

[tal-a03-v138] The seventeenth kala, therefore having the form of nectar, spreads forth through the movement of the bindu of its own higher and lower nature.

[tal-a03-v139] When devoid of visarga, that power which illuminates all things is called Shakti-Kundalini, and likewise Prana-Kundalini.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-matāntyakṣaṇavandhyāpi na pākatvaṃ prapadyate / itthaṃ prakāśatattvasya somasūryāgnitā sthitā api mukhyaṃ tatprakāśamātratvaṃ na vyapohyate / eṣāṃ yatprathamaṃ rūpaṃ hrasvaṃ tatsūrya ucyate kṣobhānandavaśāddīrghaviśrāntyā soma ucyate / yattatparaṃ plutaṃ nāma somānandātparaṃ sthitam prakāśarūpaṃ tatprāhurāgneyaṃ śāstrakovidāḥ / atra prakāśamātraṃ yatsthite dhāmatraye sati uktaṃ vindutayā śāstre śivavindurasau mataḥ / makārādanya evāyaṃ tacchāyāmātradhṛdyathā ralahāḥ ṣaṇṭhavaisargavarṇarūpatvasaṃsthitāḥ / ikāra eva rephāṃśacchāyayānyo yathā svaraḥ tathaiva mahaleśādaḥ so@nyo dvedhāsvaro@pi san / asyāntarvisisṛkṣāsau yā proktā kaulikī parā saiva kṣobhavaśādeti visargātmakatāṃ dhruvam / uktaṃ ca triśiraḥśāstre kalāvyāptyantacarcane kalā saptadaśī tasmādamṛtākārarūpiṇī / parāparasvasvarūpabindugatyā visarpitā prakāśyaṃ sarvavastūnāṃ visargarahitā tu sā / śaktikuṇḍalikā caiva prāṇakuṇḍalikā tathā

chunks.l2:
[tal-a03-v140] But at the terminal point of visarga it is called supreme Kundalini, and also the space of Shiva; it is called the supreme abode of the self of Brahman.

[tal-a03-v141] Mere visarga is the Lord's play of creation and dissolution: it is the casting of his own self into his own self, the state belonging to visarga.

[tal-a03-v142] Visarga, thus emitted and having reached a contracted state, is defined as Hamsa, as breath, as a consonant, and as a stop consonant.

[tal-a03-v143] That unsurpassed supreme abode is called Akula. The visarga of that Lord is called the Kauliki power.

[tal-a03-v144] That very same state of visarga, when bliss rises in sequence, becomes a surging forth that extends to clearly manifest action-power.

[tal-a03-v145] Visarga indeed, having drawn in so much otherness within itself, is like the ocean in this form: an endless succession of waves.

[tal-a03-v146] Therefore this visarga, consisting of the unmanifest ha and ka, is called the principle of Kama in the revered Kula cave.

[tal-a03-v147] That imperishable unmanifest, situated in the throat of the beloved, is of the nature of sound, without desire, and free from meditation and concentration.

[tal-a03-v148] Having fixed the mind there, one should subdue the world all at once. Therefore, just as visarga abides clearly in Hamsa, so too is its state understood.

[tal-a03-v149] In the same way, those beginning with Anuttara abide as the range from ka to sa. From Anuttara comes the clear emanation of the fivefold ka-group.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-visargaprāntadeśe tu parā kuṇḍalinīti ca / śivavyometi paramaṃ brahmātmasthānamucyate visargamātraṃ nāthasya sṛṣṭisaṃhāravibhramāḥ / svātmanaḥ svātmani svātmakṣepo vaisargikī sthitiḥ visarga evamutsṛṣṭa āśyānatvamupāgataḥ / haṃsaḥ prāṇo vyañjanaṃ ca sparśaśca paribhāṣyate anuttaraṃ paraṃ dhāma tadevākulamucyate / visargastasya nāthasya kaulikī śaktirucyate visargatā ca saivāsyā yadānandodayakramāt / spaṣṭībhūtakriyāśaktiparyantā procchalatsthitiḥ visarga eva tāvānyadākṣiptaitāvadātmakaḥ / iyadrūpaṃ sāgarasya yadanantormisaṃtatiḥ ata eva visargo@yamavyaktahakalātmakaḥ / kāmatattvamiti śrīmatkulaguhvara ucyate yattadakṣaramavyakta kāntākaṇṭhe vyavasthitam / dhvanirūpamanicchaṃ tu dhyānadhāraṇavarjitam tatra cittaṃ samādhāya vaśayedyugapajjagat / ata eva visargasya haṃse yadvatsphuṭā sthitiḥ tadvatsānuttarādīnāṃ kādisāntatayā sthitiḥ / anuttarātkavargasya sūtiḥ pañcātmanaḥ sphuṭam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a03-v150] Because it is necessarily of the nature of the five powers, this is clear in each case, as the power of will, abiding in its own nature, appears from a single form.

[tal-a03-v151] The ca-group is of the nature of the five powers and consists of gradual clear manifestation. Then, through connection with a brief activity that shares in the stain of the knowable, the next stage arises.

[tal-a03-v152] From that twofold power are born the pair of groups beginning with ṭa and ta. But from unfolding comes the pa-group, because through it the universe is completed.

[tal-a03-v153] This, having the form of the knowable and extending up to the twenty-fifth, is clearly manifest. Because it is knowable and thus clear, this much is declared to have the form of the stop consonants.

[tal-a03-v154] And the power of will, which is twofold as stirred and unstirred, turns toward a portion of a different power and goes to the state of ya.

[tal-a03-v155] That very same power, more quickly tinged by the stain of the knowable, and turned toward what is different, goes to the state of ra and to the state of la.

[tal-a03-v156] In the same way, the twofold unfolding power, when it moves toward the power of otherness, becomes the letter va, which pours forth the essence of creation.

[tal-a03-v157] Will itself, having reached supreme bliss, is called air when joined with swiftness; through shining it becomes fire, and through firmness it becomes earth.

[tal-a03-v158] This group of four is said to be inner because it is contained within will and the other powers and abides in its own completion.

[tal-a03-v159] The joining of the same-kind powers, beginning with will, is said to be a form of agitation, and this also applies to those whose nature involves both agitation and nonagitation.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-pañcaśaktyātmatovaśa ekaikatra yathā sphuṭaḥ / icchāśakteḥ svasvarūpasaṃsthāyā ekarūpataḥ cavargaḥ pañcaśaktyātmā kramaprasphuṭatātmakaḥ / yā tūktā jñeyakāluṣyabhākkṣipracarayogataḥ dvirūpāyāstato jātaṃ ṭa-tādyaṃ vargayugmakam / unmeṣātpādivargastu yato viśvaṃ samāpyate jñeyarūpamidaṃ pañcaviṃśatyantaṃ yataḥ sphuṭam / jñeyatvātsphuṭataḥ proktametāvatsparśarūpakam icchāśaktiśca yā dvedhā kṣubhitākṣubhitatvataḥ / sā vijātīyaśaktyaṃśapronmukhī yāti yātmatām saiva śīghrataropāttajñeyakāluṣyarūṣitā / vijātīyonmukhatvena ratvaṃ latvaṃ ca gacchati tadvadunmeṣaśaktirdvirūpā vaijātyaśaktigā / vakāratvaṃ prapadyeta sṛṣṭisārapravarṣakam icchaivānuttarānandayātā śīghratvayogataḥ / vāyurityucyate vahnirbhāsanātsthairyato dharā idaṃ catuṣkamantaḥsthamata eva nigadyate / icchādyantargatatvena svasamāptau ca saṃsthiteḥ sajātīyakaśaktīnāmicchādyānāṃ ca yojanam / kṣobhātmakamidaṃ prāhuḥ kṣobhākṣobhātmanāmapi

chunks.l2:
[tal-a03-v160] When the supreme meets its own sameness, a twofold movement arises. One of these remains simply the supreme and can give rise to bliss.

[tal-a03-v161] In that joining, a clearly agitated union arises. Even here the supreme abode is present, and the second aspect also serves the purpose of bringing something forth.

[tal-a03-v162] Without agitation, the supreme nature is not sufficient. Will may lack action, or it may be tinged by what is to be willed.

[tal-a03-v163] Divided by swiftness and firmness, will becomes threefold, appearing as unopened, opening, and fully opened.

[tal-a03-v164] What is willed appears threefold within will without losing its essential form, brought forth by will's own inner heat, which is the impulse of its freedom.

[tal-a03-v165] When the triad of śa, ṣa, and sa is clearly projected outward, it stands forth; and from that, in the letter sa, the whole universe shines clearly.

[tal-a03-v166] Yogins declare that this is the immortal, supreme abode. In the cessations at the beginning and end of agitation, that very state is known as the supreme nectar.

[tal-a03-v167] In absorptions marked by the hissing sound, bliss, and the sense of true being, that very state is declared to be the supreme, undivided absolute.

[tal-a03-v168] The Blessed Lord himself taught this in the glorious Kula mystery, a text whose true name arises from the unity of power and the holder of power.

[tal-a03-v169] Out of affection, he revealed to you the poison-principle called anacka, shaped like a crow's beak-cavity and beyond meditation and concentration.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-anuttarasya sājātye bhavettu dvitayī gatiḥ / anuttaraṃ yattatraikaṃ taccedānandasūtaye prabhaviṣyati tadyoge yogaḥ kṣobhātmakaḥ sphuṭaḥ / atrāpyanuttaraṃ dhāma dvitīyamapi sūtaye na paryāptaṃ tadā kṣobhaṃ vinaivānuttarātmatā / icchā yā karmaṇā hīnā yā caiṣṭavyena rūṣitā śīghrasthairyaprabhinnena tridhā bhāvamupāgatā / anunmiṣitamunmīlatpronmīlitamiti sthitam iṣyamāṇaṃ tridhaitasyāṃ tādrūpyasyāparicyuteḥ / tadeva svoṣmaṇā svātmasvātantryapreraṇātmanā bahirbhāvya sphuṭaṃ kṣiptaṃ śa-ṣa-satritayaṃ sthitam / tata eva sakāre@sminsphuṭaṃ viśvaṃ prakāśate amṛtaṃ ca paraṃ dhāma yoginastatpracakṣate / kṣobhādyantavirāmeṣu tadeva ca parāmṛtam sītkārasukhasadbhāvasamāveśasamādhiṣu / tadeva brahma paramamavibhaktaṃ pracakṣate uvāca bhagavāneva tacchrīmatkulaguhkare / śaktiśaktimadaikātmyalabdhānvarthābhidhānake kākacañcupuṭākāraṃ dhyānadhāraṇavarjitam / viṣatattvamanackākhyaṃ tava snehātprakāśitam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a03-v170] The true principle of desire is revealed as fullness in union, and the true principle of poison is revealed as nectar when concealment falls away.

[tal-a03-v171] The pervading power is called poison because it covers the light of what does not pervade. The supreme abode is stainless in itself, but in relation to that power it appears stained.

[tal-a03-v172] Because the universe, whose nature is action-power, flashes forth from that source, will is called desire, knowledge is called poison, and action is called the goddess, the stainless one.

[tal-a03-v173] Absorption in this triad is called Śiva, Bhairava. Our teachers said that one should always become firmly established in that state.

[tal-a03-v174] Having entered the poison-principle, one should shine forth with the contemplation 'I alone,' where there is no being, no poison, and no seizing force.

[tal-a03-v175] An objection is raised: if origin is said to come from the ṣaṇṭha letters, how can ṣaṇṭha-ness apply here? The answer is that in this case the ṣaṇṭha is not the producer.

[tal-a03-v176] For the will-power present there is the one that has been declared, and that very will-power produces its own task inwardly, in the form of what it desires.

[tal-a03-v177] What stands there as the cause of tinging is the object to be willed. From that aspect there is no true production; what arises from it is turbidity and its form.

[tal-a03-v178] They know the ṣaṇṭha as a collective joined with tinging from the knowable, because it does not function as a primary abode of either agitation or nonagitation.

[tal-a03-v179] Because this group of four letters shines forth through its own inner heat, Bhairava of pure nature declared its name to be ūṣma.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-kāmasya pūrṇatā tattvaṃ saṃghaṭṭe pravibhāvyate / viṣasya cāmṛtaṃ tattvaṃ chādyatve@ṇoścyute sati vyāptrī śaktirviṣaṃ yasmādavyāptuśchādayenmahaḥ / nirañjanaṃ paraṃ dhāma tattvaṃ tasya tu sāñjanam kriyāśaktyātmakaṃ viśvamayaṃ tasmātsphuredyataḥ / icchā kāmo viṣaṃ jñānaṃ kriyā devī nirañjanam etattrayasamāveśaḥ śivo bhairava ucyate / atra rūḍhiṃ sadā kuryāditi no guravo jaguḥ viṣatattve saṃpraviśya na bhūtaṃ na viṣaṃ na ca / grahaḥ kevala evāhamiti bhāvanayā sphuret nanvatra ṣaṇṭhavarṇebhyo janmoktaṃ tena ṣaṇṭhatā / kathaṃ syāditi cedbrūmo nātra ṣaṇṭhasya sotṛtā tathāhi tatragā yāsāvicchāśaktirudīritā / saiva sūte svakartavyamantaḥsthaṃ sveṣṭarūpakam yattvatra rūṣaṇāhetureṣitavyaṃ sthitaṃ tataḥ / bhāgānna prasavastajjaṃ kāluṣyaṃ tadvapuśca tat jñeyārūṣaṇayā yuktaṃ samudāyātmakaṃ viduḥ / ṣaṇṭhaṃ kṣobhakatākṣobhadhāmatvābhāvayogataḥ etadvarṇacatuṣkasya svoṣmaṇābhāsanāvaśāt / ūṣmeti kathitaṃ nāma bhairaveṇāmalātmanā

chunks.l2:
[tal-a03-v180] The wise say that the phonemes from ka to ha are the support of agitation; when that too is joined in the form of the womb, it moves into a further agitation.

[tal-a03-v181] Through that indication, the fiftieth phoneme arises, well established as before in the level known as the twenty-fifth.

[tal-a03-v182] There are two tetrads, in sequence, moving in difference and non-difference; the first tetrad is skilled in joining together the divisions of consciousness.

[tal-a03-v183] The other tetrad is the sole cause by which difference becomes established within non-difference; thus, whatever collection of phonemes there is, all of it was originally made of vowels.

[tal-a03-v184] A consonant becomes manifest through articulation, but its life-breath is the vowel; indeed, in the whole stream of phonemes, the root is only the group of six vowels.

[tal-a03-v185] Those six deities are the principal rays of the sun, and within those very solar rays there is a lunar digit.

[tal-a03-v186] Therefore the triad of long vowels is clearly a lunar body; and the moon is nothing other than the enjoyable and the enjoyer—there is no third thing apart from them.

[tal-a03-v187] The enjoyer alone becomes established as twofold by appearing as the enjoyable; for a pot does not have enjoyability as its own nature—rather, that belongs to the subject.

[tal-a03-v188] Therefore, the establishment that occurs in the subject is called the object's enjoyability; the unsurpassed appears through the states of being the object of awareness and the subject of awareness.

[tal-a03-v189] The enjoyable—will and the rest—attains the form of a collision; likewise, when will and the other powers rest on the ground of unsurpassed bliss, they become enjoyable.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-kādi-hāntamidaṃ prahuḥ kṣobhādhāratayā budhāḥ / yonirūpeṇa tasyāpi yoge kṣobhāntaraṃ vrajet tannidarśanayogena pañcāśattamavarṇatā / pañcaviṃśakasaṃjñeyaprāgvadbhūmisusaṃsthitam catuṣkaṃ ca catuṣkaṃ ca bhedābhedagataṃ kramāt / ādyaṃ catuṣkaṃ saṃvitterbhedasaṃdhānakovidam bhedasyābhedarūḍhyekaheturanyaccatuṣṭayam / itthaṃ yadvarṇajātaṃ tatsarva svaramayaṃ purā vyaktiyogādvyañjanaṃ tatsvaraprāṇaṃ yataḥ kila / svarāṇāṃ ṣaṭkameveha mūlaṃ syādvarṇasaṃtatau ṣaḍdevatāstu tā eva ye mukhyāḥ sūryaraśmayaḥ / saurāṇāmeva raśmīnāmantaścāndrakalā yataḥ ato@tra dīrghatritayaṃ sphuṭaṃ cāndramasaṃ vapuḥ / candraśca nāma naivānyo bhogyaṃ bhoktuśca nāparam bhoktaiva bhogyabhāvena dvaividhyātsaṃvyavasthitaḥ / ghaṭasya na hi bhogyatvaṃ svaṃ vapurmātṛgaṃ hi tat ato mātari yā rūḍhiḥ sāsya bhogyatvamucyate / anuttaraṃ parāmṛśyaparāmarśakabhāvataḥ saṃghaṭṭarūpatāṃ prāptaṃ bhogyamicchādikaṃ tathā / anuttarānandabhuvāmicchādye bhogyatāṃ gate

chunks.l2:
[tal-a03-v190] The arising of the juncture phonemes is said to be the form of the enjoyer, and the god who is made of unsurpassed bliss is said to be the enjoyer alone.

[tal-a03-v191] Will and the rest are only the enjoyable, and for that reason they are his powers; if the enjoyable dissolves into the enjoyer, then the enjoyer becomes clearly manifest in his true reality.

[tal-a03-v192] Therefore the triad, essence of six, of consciousness-will-opening nature, that same threefold, they call Bhairava's supreme greatness.

[tal-a03-v193] That triad of the supreme lord is the full power sung; by it the universe is drawn, because in this worshipped.

[tal-a03-v194] Worship born in a cut and barren universe-power: thus this greatness is only so much, and that much is not possible.

[tal-a03-v195] Who would make a limit to the power of the unlimited? Therefore the god is supreme by freedom and supremacy.

[tal-a03-v196] Endowed with emanation power, completed as universe-formed; thus the great lord has fifty-reflection full power.

[tal-a03-v197] Reflection-self is one; indeed other powers are established in this only; the eighty-one-footed goddess will be included here.

[tal-a03-v198] In one reflection nature, sound-mass is Bhairava; by reflection-shadow and union, that same power is mother-power.

[tal-a03-v199] She is different in womb from sound-mass collision; Malini is as before ninefold reflection, having separate class nature.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-saṃdhyakṣarāṇāmudayo bhoktṛrūpaṃ ca kathyate / anuttarānandamayo devo bhoktaiva kathyate icchādikaṃ bhogyameva tata evāsya śaktitā / bhogyaṃ bhoktari līnaṃ ced bhoktā tadvastutaḥ sphuṭaḥ ataḥ ṣaṇṇāṃ trikaṃ sāraṃ cidiṣyunmeṣaṇātmakam / tadeva tritayaṃ prāhurbhairavasya paraṃ mahaḥ tattrikaṃ parameśasya pūrṇā śaktiḥ pragīyate / tenākṣiptaṃ yato viśvamato@sminsamupāsite viśvaśaktāvavacchedavandhye jātamupāsanam / ityeṣa mahimaitāvāniti tāvanna śakyate aparicchinnaśakteḥ kaḥ kuryācchaktiparicchidām / tasmādanuttaro devaḥ svācchandyānuttaratvataḥ visargaśaktiyuktatvātsaṃpanno viśvarūpakaḥ / evaṃ pañcāśadāmarśapūrṇaśaktirmaheśvaraḥ vimarśātmaika evānyāḥ śaktayo@traiva niṣṭhitāḥ / ekāśītipadā devī hyatrāntarbhāvayiṣyate ekāmarśasvabhāvatve śabdarāśiḥ sa bhairavaḥ / āmṛśyacchāyayā yogātsaiva śaktiśca mātṛkā sā śabdarāśisaṃghaṭṭādbhinnayonistu mālinī / prāgvannavatayāmarśātpṛthagvargasvarūpiṇī

chunks.l2:
[tal-a03-v200] In each reflection ascent, that same is fifty-natured; thus by sound penetration, supreme reflection is natured.

[tal-a03-v201] Shiva, as mother and father, maker, is established everywhere; emanation indeed is power; this again is as Shiva-bindu.

[tal-a03-v202] Womb-made infinite universe, he resorts to supreme selfhood in unlimited universe inner essence, in own self of the lord.

[tal-a03-v203] Supreme reflection is indeed called, marked by duality attainment, in supreme emanation self, Shiva-Shakti nonduality.

[tal-a03-v204] Supreme reflection is called I by fullness of the lord; supreme first emanation ending is power-natured.

[tal-a03-v205] In withdrawn all-universe supreme, she dissolves; that universe stands within power, she supreme in supreme.

[tal-a03-v206] That her thus, what is true, by the lord enclosure-making; by that, in Trishika treatise, power's enclosed form.

[tal-a03-v207] In consciousness shines which universe; there also indeed by consciousness; that triad has gone to compaction by pair union.

[tal-a03-v208] One only supreme form of Bhairava is I-self-natured; emanation power of Shambhu thus exists everywhere.

[tal-a03-v209] From that indeed all this bliss essence agitation; for thus in sweet song, touch, or sandalwood etc.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-ekaikāmarśarūḍhau tu saiva pañcāśadātmikā / itthaṃ nādānuvedhena parāmarśasvabhāvakaḥ śivo mātāpitṛtvena kartā viśvatra saṃsthitaḥ / visarga eva śākto@yaṃ śivabindutayā punaḥ garbhīkṛtānantaviśvaḥ śrayate@nuttarātmatām / aparicchinnaviśvāntaḥsāre svātmani yaḥ prabhoḥ parāmarśaḥ sa evokto dvayasaṃpattilakṣaṇaḥ / anuttaravisargātmaśivaśaktyadvayātmani parāmarśo nirbharatvādahamityucyate vibhoḥ / anuttarādyā prasṛtirhāntā śaktisvarūpiṇī pratyāhṛtāśeṣaviśvānuttare sā nilīyate / tadidaṃ viśvamantaḥsthaṃ śaktau sānuttare pare tattasyāmiti yatsatyaṃ vibhunā saṃpuṭīkṛtiḥ / tena śrītrīśikāśāstre śakteḥ saṃpuṭitākṛtiḥ saṃvittau bhāti yadviśvaṃ tatrāpi khalu saṃvidā / tadetattritayaṃ dvandvayogātsaṃghātatāṃ gatam ekameva paraṃ rūpaṃ bhairavasyāhamātmakam / visargaśaktiryā śaṃbhoḥ setthaṃ sarvatra vartate tata evasamasto@yamānandarasavibhramaḥ / tathāhi madhure gīte sparśe vā candanādike

chunks.l2:
[tal-a03-v210] In mediacy disappearance, which throbbing in heart is bliss power; that same called, because heartful person.

[tal-a03-v211] First, having abandoned all duty in void fire, mind-rest named, then after that.

[tal-a03-v212] Toward seen, heard, etc. things in own consciousness, mind awakening called, Shakti-joy fullness natured.

[tal-a03-v213] There towardness, that thing collision of thing; in heart, of rising; by fullness entry, limited mind dissolution in Shiva.

[tal-a03-v214] As before future towardness possible limited dissolution from, mind dissolution named this, emanation Shambhava supreme.

[tal-a03-v215] In essence protection rite thus, emanation triad is said; in heart lotus sheath middle, those two collision is desired.

[tal-a03-v216] The visarga at the end is said to be the mark of the mind's rest; the second visarga is the mark of the mind's awakening.

[tal-a03-v217] When this moving and unmoving world becomes one, it shines here; indeed, some difference between object and subject is expected here.

[tal-a03-v218] Then that [reality] is called whole, yet partless through Śiva-yoga, being of the nature of a complete grasping that interrupts object and subject.

[tal-a03-v219] The third is indeed that visarga: subtle, of unity-being nature, marked by the dissolution of mind, the consciousness-self completed in itself.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-mādhyasthyavigame yāsau hṛdaye spandamānatā / ānandaśaktiḥ saivoktā yataḥ sahṛdayo janaḥ pūrva visṛjyasakalaṃ kartavyaṃ śūnyatānale / cittaviśrāntisaṃjño@yamāṇavastadanantaram dṛṣṭaśrutāditadvastupronmukhatvaṃ svasaṃvidi / cittasaṃbodhanāmoktaḥ śāktollāsabharātmakaḥ tatronmukhatvatadvastusaṃghaṭṭādvastuno hṛdi / rūḍheḥ pūrṇatayāveśānmitacittalayācchive prāgvadbhaviṣyadaunmukhyasaṃbhāvyamitatālayāt / cittapralayanāmāsau visargaḥ śāmbhavaḥ paraḥ tattvarakṣāvidhāne@to visargatraidhamucyate / hṛtpadmakośamadhyasthastayoḥ saṃghaṭṭa iṣyate visargo@ntaḥ sa ca proktaścittaviśrāntilakṣaṇaḥ / dvitīyaḥ sa visargastu cittasaṃbodhalakṣaṇaḥ ekībhūtaṃ vibhātyatra jagadetaccarācaram / grāhyagrāhakabhedo vai kiṃcidatreṣyate yadā tadāsau sakalaḥ prokto niṣkalaḥ śivayogataḥ / grāhyagrāhakavicchittisaṃpūrṇagrahaṇātmakaḥ tṛtīyaḥ sa visargastu cittapralayalakṣaṇaḥ / ekībhāvātmakaḥ sūkṣmo vijñānātmātmanirvṛtaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a03-v220] In the doctrine of Śrī Siddhayogīśvarī, the ascertained meaning is this: here Kuṇḍalinī is the seed, a living being of conscious nature.

[tal-a03-v221] The triad born from that, called the unfolding of steady desire; then letters again; the phase extends from the letter a up to vaisargikī.

[tal-a03-v222] The phonemes from ka to sa, together with the fivefold visarga, are both outside and inside, in the heart, in sound, and in the supreme state.

[tal-a03-v223] The bindu in the self pervades from the heart to the head; indeed, mantras lacking first and last would be like an autumn cloud.

[tal-a03-v224] The teacher's characteristic is this much—beginning and end—and he should know that the venerable one is like 'so'ham', a knower, Bhairava, of divine nature.

[tal-a03-v225] Whatever verse, gāthā, or the like is joined with beginning and end, therefore, knowing thus, one sees all as mantra indeed.

[tal-a03-v226] In the Vedanta called Aitareya, the Supreme Lord has ascertained in detail that the visarga-power of the universe is its cause.

[tal-a03-v227] That which is red is fire; its vigor is sun-and-moon-bodied; thus the letter 'a' is supreme Brahman, whose nature is the arising of that collision.

[tal-a03-v228] That seed too has a supreme vital power made of the five elements. As something to be enjoyed it takes the form of food, consisting of sound, touch, and taste.

[tal-a03-v229] Sound too is sweet because it increases vital power. That vital power is supreme and pure, and it is understood to have the nature of a desire to emit.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-nirūpito@yamarthaḥ śrīsiddhayogīśvarīmate / sātra kuṇḍalinī bījaṃ jīvabhūtā cidātmikā tajjaṃ dhruvecchonmeṣākhyaṃ trikaṃ varṇāstataḥ punaḥ / ā ityavarṇādityādiyāvadvaisargikī kalā kakārādisakārāntā visargātpañcadhā sa ca / bahiścāntaśca hṛdaye nāde@tha parame pade bindurātmani mūrdhāntaṃ hṛdayādvyāpako hi saḥ / ādimāntyavihīnāstu mantrāḥ syuḥ śaradabhravat gurorlakṣaṇametāvadādimāntyaṃ ca vedayet / pūjyaḥ so@hamiva jñānī bhairavo devatātmakaḥ ślokagāthādi yatkiṃcidādimāntyayutaṃ tataḥ / tasmādvidaṃstathā sarvaṃ mantratvenaiva paśyati visargaśaktirviśvasya kāraṇaṃ ca nirūpitā / aitareyākhyavedānte parameśena vistarāt yallohitaṃ tadagniryadvīryaṃ sūryenduvigraham / a iti brahma paramaṃ tatsaṃghaṭṭodayātmakam tasyāpi ca paraṃ vīrya pañcabhūtakalātmakam / bhogyatvenānnarūpaṃ ca śabdasparśarasātmakam śabdo@pi madhuro yasmādvīryopacayakārakaḥ / taddhi vīryaṃ paraṃ śuddhaṃ visisṛkṣātmakaṃ matam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a03-v230] That vital power is strength, vigor, the vital breaths, and loveliness. From it offspring arise, and it is also spoken of in ritual acts.

[tal-a03-v231] In sacrifice and other rites, in rain, in plants, again in vital power, and then in offspring, the same power circulates. Thus emission takes on the form of the whole universe.

[tal-a03-v232] That whole mass of sound is called Matrika. Because it enters a state of being both stirred and stirring, it is also declared to be Malini.

[tal-a03-v233] Malini, beautiful through the union of seed and womb and the rise of emission, is indeed determined to be the supreme power that takes the form of the whole universe.

[tal-a03-v234] In reality this supreme power is one alone and draws forth time. Yet through its connection with the differentiation of the power-holder, it takes on the form of a pair.

[tal-a03-v235] That reflective awareness, whose nature is the perfect I, abides in its own self and, by its freedom, manifests division within itself.

[tal-a03-v236] When division appears, this awareness is said to take a threefold body: Pashyanti, Madhyama, and the gross level called Vaikhari.

[tal-a03-v237] Each of those three also has a threefold form: gross, subtle, and supreme. Among them is a form beautiful with flowing tones, having the nature of sound.

[tal-a03-v238] That gross aspect is indeed Pashyanti. Since letters and other divisions have not yet appeared there, its single undivided form is called sweetness and power.

[tal-a03-v239] Clearness and harshness arise from the friction of articulatory place, breath, and so on. Yet in this sound-form they function in close proximity to consciousness.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tadbalaṃ ca tadojaśca te prāṇāḥ sā ca kāntatā / tasmādvīryātprajāstāśca vīrya karmasu kathyate yajñādikeṣu tadvṛṣṭau sauṣadhīṣvatha tāḥ punaḥ / vīrye tacca prajāsvevaṃ visarge viśvarūpatā śabdarāśiḥ sa evokto mātṛkā sāca kīrtitā / kṣobhyakṣobhakatāveśānmālinīṃ tāṃ pracakṣate bījayonisamāpattivisargodayasundarā / mālinī hi parā śaktirnirṇītā viśvarūpiṇī eṣā vastuta ekaiva parā kālasya karṣiṇī / śaktimadbhedayogena yāmalatvaṃ prapadyate tasya pratyavamarśo yaḥ paripūrṇo@hamātmakaḥ / sa svātmani svatantratvādvibhāgamavabhāsayet vibhāgābhāsane cāsya tridhā vapurudāhṛtam / paśyantī madhyamā sthūlā vaikharītyabhiśabditam tāsāmapi tridhā rūpaṃ sthūlasūkṣmaparatvataḥ / tatra yā svarasandarbhasubhagā nādarūpiṇī sā sthūlā khalu paśyantī varṇādyapravibhāgataḥ / avibhāgaikarūpatvaṃ mādhuryaṃ śaktirucyate sthānavāyvādigharṣotthā sphuṭataiva ca pāruṣī / tadasyāṃ nādarūpāyāṃ saṃvitsavidhavṛttitaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a03-v240] Absorption into that same sound is perceived suddenly. Those who do not become absorbed in it remain sunk in the body and similar limitations.

[tal-a03-v241] Those who do not know remain with their awareness sunk and not centered in the heart. For them, the sound that comes from a skin-covered drum or the like is just an external resonance.

[tal-a03-v242] Because it is both clear and unclear, that gross form is Madhyama. Madhyama also contains an undivided aspect, which is described as its coloration.

[tal-a03-v243] Where sound is made of undivided tones, it is delighting. Non-division brings fulfillment, as can be seen in the recitation of rhythm.

[tal-a03-v244] One feels satisfied in that unmanifest sound during musical playing. Yet that same level can also serve as the cause for the arising of clear letters.

[tal-a03-v245] That gross level is Vaikhari, whose function is mainly sentences and other articulated speech. Even within this gross triad there is a connecting awareness like the first.

[tal-a03-v246] When that triad is taken separately, it is called subtle. It is seen in experiences like 'I make the note shadja,' 'I play sweetly,' and 'I speak words.'

[tal-a03-v247] A threefold connecting awareness is indeed experienced separately. Of that triad, the first aspect is a form without limiting condition.

[tal-a03-v248] That is the supreme triad. There Shiva is of the nature of supreme consciousness, and in the manifestation of division three principal powers appear.

[tal-a03-v249] The three principal powers are Anuttara as supreme will, the power situated as supreme-and-non-supreme, and the unfolding power called knowledge, which is declared as the lower.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-sājātyāntarma[ttama] yībhūtirjhagityevopalabhyate / yeṣāṃ na tanmayībhūtiste dehādinimajjanam avidanto magnasaṃvinmānāstvahṛdayā iti / yattucarmāvanaddhādi kiṃcittatraiṣa yo dhvaniḥ sa sphuṭāsphuṭarūpatvānmadhyamā sthūlarūpiṇī / madhyāyāścāvibhāgāṃśasadbhāva iti raktatā avibhāgasvaramayī yatra syāttatsurañjakam / avibhāgo hi nirvṛtyai dṛśyatāṃ tālapāṭhataḥ kilāvyaktadhvanau tasminvādane parituṣyati / yā tu sphuṭānāṃ varṇānāmutpattau kāraṇaṃ bhavet sā sthūlā vaikharī yasyāḥ kāryaṃ vākyādi bhūyasā / asminsthūlatraye yattadanusandhānamādivat pṛthakpṛthaktattritayaṃ sūkṣmamityabhiśabdyate / ṣaḍjaṃ karomi madhuraṃ vādayāmi bruve vacaḥ pṛthagevānusandhānatrayaṃ saṃvedyate kila / etasyāpi trayasyādyaṃ yadrupamanupādhimat tatparaṃ tritayaṃ tatra śivaḥ paracidātmakaḥ / vibhāgābhāsanāyāṃ ca mukhyāstisro@tra śaktayaḥ anuttarā parecchā ca parāparatayā sthitā / unmeṣaśaktirjñānākhyā tvapareti nigadyate

chunks.l2:
[tal-a03-v250] From the stirring of those powers, six immaculate cognitions are declared. They arise from the immersion of those same powers as the power of action.

[tal-a03-v251] Twelve cognitions are declared, and in them all is contained. This is the principal wheel of powers of the God of gods.

[tal-a03-v252] To this extent, the God of gods, Bhairava, possessed of full power, is of the nature of reflective awareness and is united with emission and projection.

[tal-a03-v253] Because of knowledge that measures limitation, these powers are called Kalikas in some places; and in the revered Sara scripture, the supreme one-syllabled power is said to be in the middle.

[tal-a03-v254] One should worship the power called the Bhairava-self, surrounded by twelve yoginis; from them the circle of powers extends up to sixty-four.

[tal-a03-v255] Beginning from the syllable e, it unfolds up to the thousand-spoked; and in the scripture these powers are given many names according to their different functions.

[tal-a03-v256] Their modes of worship, in dual, nondual, and mixed forms, have been explained at great length in the revered Traishira.

[tal-a03-v257] It is not written here, for fear of prolixity and because it is not needed; those same powers are proclaimed as stainless, pure, and not-terrible.

[tal-a03-v258] Because they are the source of the terrible and more terrible forms, they are also of that nature, appearing in creation, maintenance, dissolution, and in the transcendence of those three conditions.

[tal-a03-v259] The abiding form of those same powers is divided in many ways, but the teachers say that the form beyond limiting conditions is twofold.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-kṣobharūpātpunastāsāmuktāḥ ṣaṭ saṃvido@malāḥ / āsāmeva samāveśātkriyāśaktitayoditāt saṃvido dvādaśa proktā yāsu sarvaṃ samāpyate / etāvaddevadevasya mukhyaṃ tacchakticakrakam etāvatā devadevaḥ pūrṇaśaktiḥ sa bhairavaḥ / parāmarśātmakatvena visargākṣepayogataḥ iyattākalanājjñānāttāḥ proktāḥ kālikāḥ kvacit / śrīsāraśāstre cāpyuktaṃ madhya ekākṣarāṃ parām pūjayedbhairavātmākhyāṃ yoginīdvādaśāvṛtām / tābhya eva catuḥṣaṣṭiparyantaṃ śakticakrakam ekārataḥ samārabhya sahasrāraṃ pravartate / tāsāṃ ca kṛtyabhedena nāmāni bahudhāgame upāsāśca dvayādvaitavyāmiśrākārayogataḥ / śrīmattraiśirame tacca kathitaṃ vistarādbahu iha no likhitaṃ vyāsabhayāccānupayogataḥ / tā eva nirmalāḥ śuddhā aghorāḥ parikīrtitāḥ ghoraghoratarāṇāṃ tu sotṛtvācca tadātmikāḥ / sṛṣṭau sthitau ca saṃhāre tadupādhitrayātyaye tāsāmeva sthitaṃ rūpaṃ bahudhā pravibhajyate / upādhyatītaṃ yadrūpaṃ taddvidhā guravo jaguḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a03-v260] This may be because limiting conditions do not arise, or because they are calmed; and that calming is twofold, either by quieting or by the method of forceful ripening.

[tal-a03-v261] The pacification called forceful ripening, fully active through the continual blazing savor of devouring, is the one fit for instruction, because it burns up the fuel of difference.

[tal-a03-v262] When all things are forcefully offered into the fire of one's own awareness, they kindle that fire by their own power and abandon the division of difference.

[tal-a03-v263] When, by forceful ripening, the divided forms of things are dissolved, the goddesses of consciousness consume the whole universe as it becomes nectar.

[tal-a03-v264] Satisfied, they repose without difference upon the god Bhairava, the sky of consciousness, who rests solely in the full heart of their own self.

[tal-a03-v265] Thus, because of their entry into various acts and functions and because of the many names and forms of worship, their manifold form appears even within non-difference.

[tal-a03-v266] And of these very goddesses, through the joining of invocation and dismissal, there is an expansion by groups of one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, and more.

[tal-a03-v267] The extensive division beginning with Rudra, Arka, Anya, Kala, Sena, and so on is vast; enough of further detail—now the discussion turns to the matter at hand.

[tal-a03-v268] This whole expanded group of things shines in the self of consciousness as a reflection; one for whom it appears thus is indeed the Lord of the universe.

[tal-a03-v269] One in whom such a non-conceptual reflective awareness is ever arising in the self is indeed marked by the Shambhava means.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-anullāsādupādhīnāṃ yadvā praśamayogataḥ / praśamaśca dvidhā śāntyā haṭhapākakrameṇa tu alaṃ grāsarasākhyena satataṃ jvalanātmanā / haṭhapākapraśamanaṃ yattṛtīyaṃ tadeva ca / upadeśāya yujyeta bhedendhanavidāhakam nijabodhajaṭharahutabhuji bhāvāḥ sarve samarpitā haṭhataḥ / vijahati bhedavibhāgaṃ nijaśaktyā taṃ samindhānāḥ haṭhapākena bhāvānāṃ rūpe bhinne vilāpite / aśnantyamṛtasādbhūtaṃ viśvaṃ saṃvittidevatāḥ tāstṛptāḥ svātmanaḥ pūrṇa hṛdayaikāntaśāyinam / cidvyomabhairavaṃ devamabhedenādhiśerate evaṃ kṛtyakriyāveśānnāmopāsābahutvataḥ / āsāṃ bahuvidhaṃ rūpamabhede@pyavabhāsate āsāmeva ca devīnāmāvāpodvāpayogataḥ / ekadvitricatuṣpañcaṣaṭsaptāṣṭanavottaraiḥ rudrārkānyakalāsenāprabhṛtirbhedavistaraḥ / alamanyena bahunā prakṛte@tha niyujyate saṃvidātmani viśvo@yaṃ bhāvavargaḥ prapañcavān / pratibimbatayā bhāti yasya viśveśvaro hi saḥ evamātmani yasyedṛgavikalpaḥ sadodayaḥ / parāmarśaḥ sa evāsau śāṃbhavopāyamudritaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a03-v270] This is the reflective awareness of full I-ness that has been explained; here there are no other practices such as mantra, mudra, ritual action, or worship.

[tal-a03-v271] Resorting again and again to this non-conceptual immersion, one attains the state of Bhairava, also called liberation while living.

[tal-a03-v272] From this point onward, liberation while living is examined, where even in brief outline the distinction between means and goal is set forth.

[tal-a03-v273] But in the previous chapter there was not even a notion of difference; therefore, in that means-less path, who is liberated, how, or from what?

[tal-a03-v274] In the non-conceptual reflective awareness called the Shambhava means, the wise person should apply the fiftyfold division that was indicated earlier.

[tal-a03-v275] Seeing even the earth itself, without conceptualization, as reflected in one's own self, one attains Bhairava-hood; the same method applies to water and the other elements as well.

[tal-a03-v276] At the final limit, one conceives a supreme principle beyond all coverings, all-pervading, independent, all-knowing, and called Shiva.

[tal-a03-v277] Seeing even that conceived Shiva reflected in the mirror of unconstructed, noble awareness, and free from conceptual thought, one becomes Bhairava oneself.

[tal-a03-v278] Just as one who sees a red object in front with nonconceptual awareness becomes firmly established in the undivided awareness of that one pot through its various channels.

[tal-a03-v279] In the same way, recognizing one's own self through each and every aggregate beginning with earth, one shines forth as truly full.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-pūrṇāhantāparāmarśo yo@syāyaṃ pravivecitaḥ / mantramudrākriyopāsāstadanyā nātra kāścana bhūyobhūyaḥ samāveśaṃ nirvikalpamimaṃ śritaḥ / abhyeti bhairavībhāvaṃ jīvanmuktyaparābhidham ita eva prabhṛtyeṣā jīvanmuktirvicāryate / yatra sūtraṇayāpīyamupāyopeyakalpanā prāktane tvāhnike kācidbhedasya kalanāpi no / tenānupāye tasminko mucyate vā kathaṃ kutaḥ nirvikalpe parāmarśe śāmbhavopāyanāmani / pañcāśadbhedatāṃ pūrvasūtritāṃ yojayedbudhaḥ dharāmevāvikalpena svātmani pratibimbitām / paśyanbhairavatāṃ yāti jalādiṣvapyayaṃ vidhiḥ yāvadante paraṃ tattvaṃ samastāvaraṇordhvagam / vyāpi svatantraṃ sarvajñaṃ yacchivaṃ parikalpitam tadapyakalpitodārasaṃviddarpaṇabimbitam / paśyanvikalpavikalo bhairavībhavati svayam yathā raktaṃ puraḥ paśyannirvikalpakasaṃvidā / tattaddvāraniraṃśaikaghaṭasaṃvittisusthitaḥ tadvaddharādikaikaikasaṃghātasamudāyataḥ / parāmṛśansvamātmānaṃ pūrṇa evāvabhāsate

chunks.l2:
[tal-a03-v280] This has arisen from me, this is reflected in me alone, and this is not different from me: in this threefold way is the Shambhava means.

[tal-a03-v281] This is the summary of creation, maintenance, and withdrawal. As it is established and taught, the Spanda teaching states it.

[tal-a03-v282] By this alone the supreme sovereign nature of awareness and its identity as the self of all are made known; what other defining mark need be stated?

[tal-a03-v283] In my own self, in the space of consciousness, I manifest the universe; through this expansive recognition as the creator whose self is the universe, Bhairava identity unfolds.

[tal-a03-v284] The entire group of the six paths is reflected in me alone; recognizing 'I am the maker of maintenance' is this clear universal form.

[tal-a03-v285] Seeing that this universe melts in me, in the self matted with the flames of ever-risen great awakening, one becomes still.

[tal-a03-v286] I am Shiva, the exulting fire that burns the dream-house of samsara, filled with endless varied beings.

[tal-a03-v287] The whole world arises from me in many differentiated forms, yet when it dissolves in me no other remains. One who sees creation, maintenance, and dissolution as play in a partless reality shines forth in the fourth state.

[tal-a03-v288] In that supreme means, abounding in Shaiva non-duality, some indeed attain trust, being cultivated by the lord of bound souls.

[tal-a03-v289] Bathing, vow, body purification, retention, mantra application, path arrangement, sacrifice rite, offering, recitation, and concentration.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-matta evoditamidaṃ mayyeva pratibimbitam / madabhinnamidaṃ ceti tridhopāyaḥ sa śāmbhavaḥ sṛṣṭeḥ sthiteḥ saṃhṛteśca tadetatsūtraṇaṃ kṛtam / yatra sthitaṃ yataśceti tadāha spandaśāsane etāvataiva hyaiśvarya saṃvidaḥ khyāpitaṃ param / viśvātmakatvaṃ cetyanyallakṣaṇaṃ kiṃ nu kathyatām svātmanyeva cidākāśe viśvamasmyavabhāsayan / sraṣṭā viśvātmaka iti prathayā bhairavātmatā ṣaḍadhvajātaṃ nikhilaṃ mayyeva pratibimbitam / sthitikartāhamasmīti sphuṭeyaṃ viśvarūpatā sadoditamahābodhajvālājaṭilatātmani / viśvaṃ dravati mayyetaditi paśyanpraśāmyati anantacitrasadgarbhasaṃsārasvapnasadmanaḥ / ploṣakaḥ śiva evāhamityullāsī hutāśanaḥ jagatsarvaṃ mattaḥ prabhavati vibhedena bahudhā tathāpyetadrūḍhaṃ mayi vigalite tvatra na paraḥ / taditthaṃ yaḥ sṛṣṭisthitivilayabhekīkṛtivaśādanaṃśaṃ paśyetsa sphurati hi turīyaṃ padabhitaḥ tadasminparamopāye śāmbhavādvaitaśālini / ke@pyeva yānti viśvāsaṃ pasmeśena bhāvitāḥ snānaṃ vrataṃ dehaśuddhirdhāraṇā mantrayojanā / adhvaklṛptiryāgavidhirhomajapyasamādhayaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a03-v290] Such imaginings are not fitted here by difference; the grace-causing state of one present here is clearly established.

[tal-a03-v291] If one worthy of such grace approaches the teacher, then he is such; he would not be through devotion to becoming, but cultivated.

[tal-a03-v292] He worships him; then, from the cultivated grace-giver, he should learn the various initiation rites.

[tal-a03-v293] Future ones too have those devotions; they attain completion, and this essence-state, supreme and to be obtained, is described as Shiva.

[tal-a03-v294] Thus this supreme Shaiva self-knowledge has been told in great detail.
